clue.text: Fail when beginning to talk — it's hot air

parts.note: to bomb is to flop or fail badly
as in 'as I arrived' means when I arrived

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: first letter of talk

explanation.surface: A speaker who flops as soon as they open their mouth is just producing hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated language with little substance, which is what hot air means figuratively.

clue.text: Well-oiled machine run by 25's team

parts.note: surface reading: a smoothly running engine, or perhaps a drunk one
setter's reading: the slick football club that 25 (Der Kaiser) played for and later ran as president

explanation.surface: A smoothly lubricated engine is operated by some team.
explanation.walkthrough: Der Kaiser (25) is Franz Beckenbauer, who captained and later presided over the German club; 'well-oiled machine' is a cliché for an efficient football side, with a nod to the beer of Munich.
explanation.definitionFit: The German football club, famed for efficiency, was Beckenbauer's club as player, coach and president.

clue.text: See 1
Raab corrected says these are LAS countries

indicators.note: a correction puts things into a different, proper order

parts.note: the name taken as written, to be rearranged
to state is to say

explanation.surface: The politician Dominic Raab is put right on which countries belong to some organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: LAS is the League of Arab States, the regional body of Middle Eastern and North African nations.
explanation.definitionFit: The members of the League of Arab States are, naturally, Arab states; the definition describes them by their membership.

clue.text: Monster to walk slowly after beheading

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the head, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: to stroll is to walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: A monster forced to shuffle along once it has had its head cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: A troll is an ugly giant or dwarf of Scandinavian folklore, a kind of monster.

clue.text: Sappers leaving one French city for base

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: whatever leaves is taken out of the word it was in

parts.note: the city in the French Alps
the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are nicknamed sappers

explanation.surface: Army engineers pull out of a French city and head to their base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' seems to be a military camp, but here it is the adjective meaning dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Base as an adjective means morally low or dishonourable, a synonym of ignoble.

clue.text: Tees is ready: solver reportedly unprepared!

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken or heard, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: Tees is the setter, so in their voice 'I'm prompt', followed by the solver addressed as 'you'

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being ready and teases the solver for being caught off guard.
explanation.walkthrough: Tees is this puzzle's setter, so 'Tees is' becomes I AM, and the solver is you.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done on the spur of the moment, without preparation or rehearsal.

clue.text: Ham producer's Japanese production around area

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese masked drama
standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A Japanese food company is making ham in some region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham producer' looks like a pig farmer; in Genesis Ham is a son of the ark builder.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Noah fathered three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, so he 'produced' Ham.

clue.text: Recording device in jet pack

parts.note: jet is a deep black, as in jet-black
to pack something is to box it

explanation.surface: A recording device is stowed inside an aircraft's equipment pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' reads as an aircraft, which fits the answer's world perfectly, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's flight recorder, which logs data and cockpit sound, is popularly called by this name.

clue.text: Former barrister killing time sees model

parts.note: ex- means former

indicators.note: killing something removes it, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a Templar is a lawyer of the Inner or Middle Temple in London
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A retired lawyer who murders time has become a role model.
explanation.walkthrough: Templar for a barrister comes from the Inns of Court called the Temple, where many London barristers have chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a person or thing serving as a model or typical example to be copied.

clue.text: Yiddish gossip truly accepting Christian work

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: yea is an archaic word for truly or indeed
the New Testament, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A gossip who admits to being impressed by some religious writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Yenta is a Yiddish-derived word for a busybody or meddling gossip, usually a woman.

clue.text: Hotel specialist returned to run leaderless institution

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so it is read from right to left

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pro is a professional or expert

indicators.note: without a leader means the word has lost its first letter

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: A hotel expert came back to run a care home that had lost its head.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is a residential institution caring for children without parents.

clue.text: Fish surprises, served with nut endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: to rock someone is to shock or surprise them
an almond is a nut

explanation.surface: A fish dish arrives with a surprise garnish of nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock salmon is a British fish-and-chip shop name for dogfish or similar fish, not a true salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salmon is a trade name for dogfish and other fish sold in British chip shops.

clue.text: Don't go to sleep with Stheno at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the name before it

parts.note: first letter of Stheno
kip is British slang for sleep

explanation.surface: A warning not to nod off near Stheno, a Gorgon whose gaze is deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Stheno is one of the three Gorgons, sister of Medusa; only her initial is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip a class or meeting is to deliberately not attend it.

clue.text: Finished plans for lending arrangements

parts.note: something over is finished
drafts are preliminary plans or sketches

explanation.surface: Plans have been completed for some loan agreements.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdraft is a facility letting a bank customer borrow by spending beyond their balance, a form of lending.

clue.text: Dancer in Opal van — a van wrecked

indicators.note: a wrecked thing is smashed apart and its parts lie jumbled

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer riding in a Vauxhall Opal van, which then gets wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Pavlova was a celebrated Russian prima ballerina, famous for The Dying Swan.

clue.text: Spray where blue rinse needs management

definitions.note: the answer is the device that makes a fine spray

indicators.note: letters that need managing must be organised into a new order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: At the hairdresser's, a blue rinse needs careful handling with the spray.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue rinse is a hair tint associated with older women.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebuliser turns liquid medicine into a fine mist or spray to be inhaled.

clue.text: Alumnus Eliot entertaining cheeky thrusts forward

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: the initials of the poet T S Eliot
rude means impudent or cheeky

explanation.surface: A former pupil, Eliot, plays host to someone impertinent.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to push or thrust oneself or something forward, intrusively.

clue.text: Arsenic and Old Lace — synopsis needed

indicators.note: to lace a drink is to doctor it, so the letters are tampered with

parts.note: the word taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone wants a plot summary of the black comedy Arsenic and Old Lace.
explanation.walkthrough: The play title tempts you to read it whole; 'Lace' is split off as the signal, since lacing is spiking.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an outline of the plot of a play or film, a synopsis.

clue.text: See 26
King seen in hackneyed war drama

indicators.note: something seen in a phrase is sitting inside its letters

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A monarch appears in a clichéd war film.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward has been the name of several English and British kings.

clue.text: Ounce captured by farmer who likes a drink

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun 'one who likes a drink'

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor

parts.note: Boer is Afrikaans/Dutch for farmer
oz is the abbreviation for ounce

explanation.surface: A wild cat (an ounce is a snow leopard) has been caught by a hard-drinking farmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Ounce looks like the snow leopard; it is the weight abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A boozer is a heavy drinker, someone fond of alcohol; it is also British slang for a pub.

clue.text: Mysterious character in ecstasy after work

parts.note: a machine that works is said to run
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An enigmatic figure reaches bliss once the working day is done.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts are given in reverse order: 'after work' puts the drug after the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A rune is a letter of an ancient Germanic alphabet, associated with magic and mystery.

clue.text: Notice advertisement in city causing alarm?

definitions.note: describes the device by what it does; a noun is needed

parts.note: to clock something is British slang for noticing it

indicators.note: in places the preceding item inside the following one

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro
short for advertisement

explanation.surface: A notice posted around a city creates public panic.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: 'alarm' here is a wake-up sound, not fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock radio combines a clock and a radio and can be set to sound as a morning alarm.

clue.text: Canine tooth one has right in middle

indicators.note: a word that has something holds it within itself

parts.note: a cog is a tooth on a gear wheel
R is the abbreviation for right
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dog's canine tooth sits right in the middle of its mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine tooth' reads as one phrase; 'Canine' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh dog breed, so it is a canine.

clue.text: Man in suit lifting equipment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the knave, a male court card in each suit
second meaning: a device for raising a car

explanation.walkthrough: The 'suit' is of playing cards, not clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the knave in a deck of cards and a device used to raise heavy loads such as a car.

clue.text: 26 18 taking a risk when out among animals

indicators.note: among means in the midst of, so the jumble sits inside

parts.note: deer are animals

indicators.note: out here means disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer takes a chance out among the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Der Kaiser, German for the Emperor, was the nickname of the commanding footballer Franz Beckenbauer.

clue.text: Footballer, French, by an unknown stream in Parisian arbour we hear

parts.note: standard abbreviation for French
taken as written
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z
a beck is a northern English word for a stream
en is French for in

indicators.note: we hear means the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a bower is a leafy shelter; the German surname is said the same way

explanation.surface: A French footballer, beside a stream in a Paris garden bower, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' tempts as the footballer's nationality, but he was German; it only gives two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Beckenbauer was a German footballer, World Cup winner as captain and as manager.

clue.text: Rude gesture given with little hesitation in game

parts.note: to cock a snook is to thumb one's nose at someone
er is a brief hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A player makes a rude gesture after a moment's pause during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: To cock a snook is a British idiom: thumb on nose, fingers spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue sport played on a baize table with fifteen reds and six colours.

clue.text: Accepted member wearing crimson is backed

parts.note: to be in clothes is to be wearing them

indicators.note: backed here means put into reverse, so the words run right to left

parts.note: crimson is red, plus is taken as written

explanation.surface: A member of the club is dressed in red and has support.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is someone accepted within a group or organisation, with access to its private knowledge.
